BA.thesis: Boeing is the long leg of the contrarian "Long Boeing / Short Airbus" trade: the most operationally troubled US major is inflecting just as Airbus hits its first serious execution wall. CFO guided (Dec 2 UBS) to ~$2B 2025 cash burn turning to low-single-digit-billions positive FCF in 2026 (~$3B) on higher 737/787 deliveries, better defense margins, the Spirit acquisition, and deleveraging; the $10B FCF target remains the destination. Airbus cut guidance on Spirit-sourced panel defects, faces GTF groundings, a software bug, slipping rate targets and 25% US tariffs — handing Boeing's US lines a pricing edge. ~low-30s x 2026 FCF on a falling multiple, backlog sold out through the decade.
BA.source: Ported from the manager's STOXTRXR book

KLAC.thesis: process-control (metrology + inspection) near-monopoly; inspection intensity per wafer rises with node/stack complexity (HBM 12–16-Hi, 3D DRAM), so KLA’s content grows even when wafer counts don’t. | WFE = the real bottleneck (Zephyr 2030 DRAM model, Jul ’26): the memory supercycle can’t be ‘broken’ by 2030 — wafer supply only ~2× by 2030 vs customers asking 4–5×, leaving a structural ~25% conventional-DRAM deficit (~91EB supply vs ~120EB demand). HBM’s ~4× effective-wafer multiplier (bigger dies + TSV yield loss) means ~70% of Big-3 capacity is consumed by HBM, so ~2.8–3.66M WPM of incremental DRAM capacity has to be built — and equipment is THE constraint. Net: WFE is the leveraged pick-and-shovel beneficiary regardless of which memory maker wins. (Bull-modeled & promotional — citrini.com; softest input is the ~75EB ‘agentic-CPU’ demand bucket that doesn’t exist yet.)
KLAC.source: Ported from the manager's STOXTRXR book
